The story effectively balances the compression of an entire academic year (from October to late spring) with the slowing down of time during pivotal emotional moments. The author uses clear seasonal and monthly markers ("By October," "In November," "Winter dark arrived early," "In January," "By spring") to smoothly compress weeks of routine campus life and growing relationships into concise summaries. Conversely, the pacing slows down to real-time dialogue during critical turning points—such as Mara confronting Carl about his essay, Martin kissing her at the café, and Lizzy calling out her hypocrisy. This deliberate alternation allows the reader to feel the gradual passage of the school year while still experiencing the immediate weight of the scenes that drive Mara's personal growth.
